text.p: Wackenhut Corrections Corp said on Monday it bought a 224-bed prison facility in McFarland, Calif., for about $6 million.
It had been operating the prison as a return-to-custody facility for the California Department of Corrections since 1989, the company said in a statement.
Funds came from proceeds of Wackenhut's 2.3 million common stock offering earlier this year, it said.

"This equity investment is consistent with our new business strategy of increasing company earnings through targeted facility-ownership investments," George Zoley, Wackenhut president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"Our ability to do this is reinforced by our substantial cash reserves as well as an untapped banking credit line," he said.
Zoley said the strategy of buying prisons Wackenhut already managed would enhance earnings potential.
The 35,000 square foot building in McFarland was built in 1988 and was situated on five acres of land, it said.
